title: Japan 30-Year JGB auction (¥600bn anticipated, reopening of issue 91) — the pivot of the super-long curve, and the same date the US sells its own 30-year
source: EST: mof.go.jp English October 2026 auction calendar (policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2610e.htm), re-fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 24,853 bytes) for this initial research; its table row reads 'Oct. 8, 2026 | 30-year'. The DATE is MOF's own. The SIZE is anticipated, not announced: that row's 'Auction Announcement' cell carries NO href on 2026-09-08, where the September calendar's 09-15 20-year row already links a live announcement (announcement/auct20260908e.htm), and MOF's own note on the page reads 'Each issue amount will be announced about one week prior to each auction date' — so the confirming primary lands ~2026-10-01. The ¥600bn anticipated size and the reopening read come from two further MOF primaries: the Auction Results for JGBs workbook (english/policy/jgbs/auction/past_auction_results/Auction_Results_for_JGBs.xls, 492,032 bytes, last saved 2026-08-13, downloaded and parsed 2026-09-08), and MOF's own result pages for the two auctions the workbook does not yet carry (eresul/eresul20260806.htm and eresul20260903.htm, both HTTP 200, fetched 2026-09-08). The 30-year runs monthly (Aug. 6, Sep. 3, Oct. 8 on MOF's own calendars), MOF cut it from ¥700bn to ¥600bn effective 2026-04-07, and issue 91 (4.0% coupon, maturity 2056-06-20) has now been sold three times at ¥600bn — 2026-07-07, 08-06 and 09-03. Unlike the 40-year, the 30-year IS a multiple-price auction and does report a tail. Filed `estimate` on the same two counts every JGB entry on this calendar records: the size is anticipated rather than announced, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: Proposed 2026-09-08 by the jgb-40y-auction-2026-09-29 initial-research adjacency sweep (proposals/jgb-30y-auction-2026-10-08.from-jgb-40y-auction-2026-09-29.json, read as input and now shadowed by this canonical file); researched the same day (docs/research/events/jgb-30y-auction-2026-10-08.md). THE FRAMEWORK TRANSFERS FROM THE 20-YEAR BUT ITS CALIBRATION DOES NOT. The 30-year is multiple-price and prints a real tail — confirmed on MOF's own result pages — so unlike the 40-year it can be judged the way the 09-15 sibling judges the 20-year; but the numbers are tenor-specific. Across all 202 multiple-price 30-year auctions (2007-04-17 → 2026-09-03) the tail runs mean 0.82bp, median 0.60, sd 0.82, p90 1.69, p95 2.19, and only 7.4% reach 2bp, against 10.5% at the 20-year — and the 40-year ledger's clearing-gap threshold transplants far worse, because the 30-year clears mean +1.55bp cheap to MOF's same-session par with sd 3.79bp, so the 40-year's '+3bp = top 4%' rule would flag 44 of 202 (22%) here. MOF ALSO CONVERTED THIS TENOR ONCE: the 25 auctions from 1999-09-02 to 2007-01-18 print '―' in both average-price columns and all 200 since 2007-04-17 print real numbers, which makes the 40-year sibling's 'MOF changes the auction format' kill switch a documented precedent rather than an exotic one. THE LOAD-BEARING NEW FINDING IS A REFUTATION OF A TEST THAT LOOKS SIGNIFICANT. This is the one date on the calendar where a same-tenor foreign sovereign auction prints hours before the US one (treasury-30y-bond-2026-10-08, same date), so the spillover test finally gets its cleanest form — and it fails under control. Raw, n=197 auctions matched to the same-date US 30Y CMT: soft (tail >= 2bp, n=15) precedes +3.00bp against +0.18bp for firm, difference +2.82bp at t = +2.62, corr(tail, US move) +0.169 (t = +2.39), and it is NOT outlier-driven (dropping the three largest |US move| days raises t to +2.69; jackknifing the 15 soft observations leaves t in 2.27-2.94). But the tail is mostly a symptom of that day's own JGB selloff — corr(tail, same-date JGB 30Y par move) = +0.328, t = +4.85 — and JGB and US 30-year moves are themselves correlated (+0.208, t = +2.97); the PARTIAL correlation of the tail with the US move controlling for the same-date JGB move is +0.109 at t = +1.52, and nothing survives to the next session (D+1 corr +0.082, t = +1.15; D+2 nil). Common factor, not transmission. A SOURCED MECHANISM FOR THE CURVE SHAPE BOTH SIBLING LEDGERS MEASURED AND NEITHER EXPLAINED, closing the BoJ gap the 40-year ledger flagged as unsourced: across 16 monthly BoJ operation files 2024-01 -> 2026-08 (boj.or.jp/en/statistics/boj/fm/ope/m_release), purchases in the 'More than 25 years' bucket are FLAT at ¥150bn every single month (two operations of ¥75bn), while the 'More than 10 years and up to 25 years' bucket was tapered from ¥450bn to ¥200bn a month (-55%, operation count 3 -> 2). Because MOF cut 25y+ coupon issuance over the same window, the BoJ's share of it ROSE from ~12% to ~20% while its share of 20-year supply FELL from ~45% to ~29% — and the segment that kept its buyer is the one that did not cheapen: 20s30s stands at +25.8bp (73.7th percentile of 4,606 sessions) while 30s40s stands at +0.4bp (1.7th). The 30-year sits at the kink, rich to the 20-year and priced flat to the 40-year. Two corrections to sibling numbers, both from the same workbook: the super-long taper is deeper than recorded, 30Y ¥900bn -> ¥600bn (-33%, not the -14% on file) and 40Y ¥700bn -> ¥300bn (-57%, not -40%), because both sibling windows begin mid-taper. Two nulls banked: a flat 30s40s does not break this auction (n=48 flat-regime auctions vs 151, tail difference +0.17bp at t = 1.13, cover -0.053 at t = -0.65 — the sibling's same inference rested on n=2), and there is no October fiscal-H2 'fresh money' effect (n=19, neighbour-controlled cover +0.091 at t = +0.73, tail -0.13bp at t = -1.01, out of a pre-declared 12-month family). NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is `low`: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure, no house playbook is rates-keyed, and the one channel that could have justified an entry is the refuted one above. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
